citations.anchor: keeps the order the field declared
citations.why: asserts opsForField returns the field's declared order verbatim ([is_one_of, equals]), which is the property that distinguishes seeding the default from opsForField rather than from OPS_FOR_TYPE.

citations.anchor: opens on the multi-select, and names several audiences in one rule
citations.why: picking the audience field lands the rule on `is one of` (checkbox group, `in` on the wire); seeding from OPS_FOR_TYPE would leave it on `equals` and both the value-editor interaction and the URL assertion would fail.

citations.anchor: still refuses an operator the type does not admit
citations.why: a boolean field declaring `between` gets only `equals` back — the declaration narrows and cannot widen the type's set.
a declaration intersecting nothing falls back to the type's full set instead of returning an empty option list — the second half of the invariant.

citations.anchor: offers nothing for a type it has never heard of
citations.why: a field typed `constructor` must read back [] from OPS_FOR_TYPE; a bare index would return a truthy inherited member and this expectation fails.

?filter= carrying op `constructor`/`toString`/`valueOf`/`__proto__` must not resolve through WIRE_TO_UI: the test asserts the records table survives and no condition reaches the summary, which is exactly the `Object.hasOwn` guard on WIRE_TO_UI.

citations.anchor: count is clamped instead of crashing the panel
citations.why: typing a within_last count past the representable-instant range must clamp (asserts the input holds 100000) and leave the panel alive rather than throwing out of the live JSON preview's serialisation.
a hand-edited ?filter= with an unrecognised operator must yield a discarded rule rather than throw: the test asserts the page renders and the error boundary's 'Something went wrong' never appears.

citations.anchor: a "contains" rule wraps its value in escaped wildcards
citations.why: asserts the serialised leaf equals exactly {field, op, value} — a client-side FilterRule.id leaking into the wire JSON would fail this toEqual.
clearing every condition must leave no ?filter= at all; treeToJsonFilter answering an empty tree with {"and":[]} instead of null would put the param back and fail the not.toHaveURL(/filter=/).

citations.anchor: the Apply gate refuses a non-boolean value on a boolean field
citations.why: a hand-written invalid value must not commit — asserts the URL never gains the {"and":[…]} wrapper and the rule error is shown, i.e. the gate let nothing through.

citations.anchor: shows an error state instead of an empty picker
citations.why: with the filter-fields request failing, the panel names the failure and Apply is disabled — the invariant's second clause, that missing field definitions refuse every rule rather than leaving a dead button.

citations.anchor: an operator the field does not offer is reported without pressing Apply
citations.why: operator_not_allowed is displayed on open, before any Apply — pinning that this code ignores showErrors.

citations.anchor: the Apply gate refuses a substring operator on a date field
citations.why: an `ilike` on a datetime field (which the builder cannot draw an operator cell for) is refused at Apply — the URL keeps its hand-written shape and the rule error stands, so operator legality is checked ahead of the value.
